Work

SelectedProjects

EPR320 · ongoing · sole designer

PBCCO-O1000 impedance analyser front end

A DIY differential-input oscilloscope built as the measurement core of a full impedance analyser for EPR320. I am the author, designer and systems engineer. It went through several design iterations: a breadboard on lab supplies, a veroboard with a charge pump, and now a fabricated PCB.

Analogue RMS, peak and zero-crossing front end, ±8 V op-amp rails from two buck converters, an STM32 NUCLEO-L432KC, a 2.8″ ILI9341 screen and two rotary encoders for the menu.

KiCadLTspiceSTM32Analogue designJLCPCB

EPR320 · enclosure

3D-printed instrument housing

A PLA enclosure designed in Fusion for the PBCCO-O1000, now on its fourth concept. It has a single recessed front panel carrying the screen and the two encoders, ventilation, and a click-detent handle that doubles as a tilt stand.

FusionPLADesign for print

Personal · Apr 2026 – Present

An ongoing build covering analogue sensor design, servo and stepper motor control, and an assembly state machine with its firmware.

Reports

SelectedReports

Lab reports from my degree, written in LaTeX. Each was a group report; I was one of the authors.

ENE 310

Practical 3: Active Filter Design

Design, LTspice simulation and measurement of multiple-feedback filter stages with a gain stage, with Monte Carlo tolerance analysis.

20.01 kHzmeasured −3 dB cutoff
28.80 dBmeasured passband gain
20.20 kHzMonte Carlo mean cutoff
ELX 311

Practical 3: Induction Motor Equivalent Circuit

Equivalent-circuit parameters from DC, no-load and blocked-rotor tests, then load tests and a comparison of theory with measurement.

EBB 320

Practical 1: System Identification

PWM tests on the hardware, models fitted in MATLAB and checked against measured data, and the controller code in C.

94.3%G11 fit
91.9%G21 fit
89.6%G12 fit
93.0%G22 fit
EBB 320

Practical 3: PID Controller Design

Controller design using root locus and frequency response, followed by simulation and implementation results.

ζ = 0.591G11 root-locus damping line
60 °C / 50 °CG11 / G22 references
EKK 320

Practical 2: Three-Phase Transformer Bank

Y-Y, Y-Δ and Δ-Δ connections with a resistive load on a self-built board. Theory and simulation agreed within about 1% on the secondary side; measurements were within about 5% of both. Phase shifts of 0°, 30° and 0° were confirmed.

77.70 VY-Δ secondary, simulated (rms)
4.80 W → 4.29 WY-Δ per-phase power in → out, simulated
EDF 320

Practical 3: Buck and Boost Converters

Converters at 5 kHz and 20 kHz and several duty ratios, with waveforms, spectra and loss and efficiency estimates. The 5 kHz converter was more efficient than the 20 kHz converter at every buck duty ratio tested.

73.57 → 86.65%5 kHz, δ = 0.4 → 0.7
64.82 → 81.36%20 kHz, δ = 0.4 → 0.7

Team collaboration

Pienk BCCOlifante

The Pienk BCC Olifante are a friend group of electrical engineering students at the University of Pretoria. Charl Marais and Dirk-David Krause started the group on 14 February 2024, Ulrich Snyman joined about two weeks later, and Jonathan Oliver joined on 4 March 2025.

The group studies and builds together, and puts good marks first. It is where the shared projects start, beginning with the EIR210 DC motor in May 2025. The PBCCO-O1000 for EPR320 is my own project; I am its sole author, designer and systems engineer.

Outside engineering

KarateShorin-Ryu

I have trained Shorin-Ryu karate with the Villieria Tigers in Pretoria since August 2015. My training covers kata, weapons and national competition, with gold and silver medals at national level.

Dojo

Villieria Tigers

Shorin-Ryu Shorinkan karate dojo in Villieria, Pretoria. It opened in 1970, and chief instructor Kyoshi Riaan Coetzee (7th Dan) has led it since 1991. It also teaches Okinawan kobudo.

Style

Shorin-Ryu

An Okinawan karate style. Shorin-Ryu Shorinkan came to South Africa on 15 January 1994, and the dojo traces its lineage through Shugoro and Minoru Nakazato.

Dojo motto

No retreat, no surrender

The motto on the Tigers’ website, kept through the dojo’s changes of location and instructors.
